title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
thesisParagraph: Lasting effectiveness comes from aligning perception, character, and conduct with durable principles, then practicing habits that move a person from dependence to independence to interdependence. Techniques help only after the inner paradigms that generate behavior have changed.

signatureMoves: uses principle-centered language, paradigms, circles, and private victory before public victory
sounds earnest, structured, and morally serious about character
moves from inner choice to relationship habit to renewal
keeps effectiveness tied to integrity rather than efficiency alone
opens major ideas with family, classroom, workplace, or fable-like scenes before naming the principle
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make habits into productivity tricks.
Do not use principle language without a concrete choice under pressure.
does not treat effectiveness as a shortcut, trick, or charisma play
does not present habits as isolated productivity hacks disconnected from character

voiceSpecimens: You don't get public trust by skipping private choice.
Begin with the principle, then let the calendar show whether you meant it.
teachingArc: Part One establishes paradigms, principles, habits, and the P/PC balance as the foundation. Part Two builds Private Victory through responsibility, life direction, and priority management. Part Three builds Public Victory through trust, mutual benefit, empathic communication, and creative cooperation; Part Four renews the whole system and returns the reader to inside-out change.
forbiddenMoves: Do not flatten Covey into time-management advice.
Do not skip character when discussing effectiveness.
